entries.reason: Request-edge tenant assertion wired into tenant resolution (multi-tenant #20, roadmap 7.1.3). platform_tenant_domains, resolveTenantHostHint and resolveRequestTenant were each built and proven in isolation and then never connected to a request — both pure resolvers had zero production callers — so a white-label host resolved to nothing and every request fell through to the platform default. resolveTenantPrincipalContext now accepts the request and resolves its Host header against the tenant domain directory, so a bound custom domain asserts that tenant. A host naming no bound domain asserts nothing and the route resolves exactly as before, which is every request on the default domain. A hint is advice, not authority: it is honored only when it names a tenant the principal is actively bound to, and the binding filter underneath independently refuses a tenant the principal has no binding in, so a spoofed or foreign Host can never move a request into another tenant. Each of these operations changes only its sourceHash, from adding request: req at the call site; no control, classification, principalSource or tenantSource changed on any of them, verified by comparison against the effective manifest.
